name: Lordamere Internment Camp
summary: Surviving Dalaran magi and guards hold Lordamere Internment Camp above Dalaran. The old prison also shelters Forsaken defectors.

sections.title: From Prison to Research Outpost
sections.body: Lordamere Internment Camp now serves Dalaran’s remnants as a research outpost. After the Second War, the Alliance built camps across the northern kingdoms to hold the defeated orcish Horde. Lordamere was the only camp in the Alterac Mountains, and Dalaran oversaw it. The orcs have long since been freed or fled. Warden Belamoore leads the camp, where Dalaran’s survivors study dangerous magical relics.

sections.title: Forsaken Defectors
sections.body: Four Forsaken renegades, including Kegan Darkmar, fled to Lordamere with Bloodstone artifacts stolen from the Undercity. They traded the relics to Warden Belamoore for sanctuary behind Dalaran’s lines. The magi accepted them for arcane study. In Tarren Mill, executors send loyal Horde operatives to hunt the defectors and recover the stolen Bloodstones before Dalaran unlocks their power.

faq.q: What was this camp originally built for?
aliases: why is there a camp here
faq.answer: After the Second War, the Alliance built the camp to imprison orcs who had grown lethargic after losing their demonic bloodlust. Dalaran manned its watchtowers and oversaw it because it stood so close to the magi’s city.

faq.q: Who controls the camp right now?
faq.answer: Warden Belamoore and a detachment of Dalaran guards and magi hold the camp. Though Dalaran suffered heavy damage, its survivors continue their research from the fortified hilltop.

faq.q: Why are there undead Forsaken inside the camp?
faq.answer: Kegan Darkmar leads the deserters from the Undercity. They betrayed Queen Sylvanas and stole sacred Bloodstone artifacts, then traded the relics to Warden Belamoore for protection from Forsaken retribution.

angles.text: The deserters at Lordamere have betrayed the Dark Lady. Hunting Kegan Darkmar and recovering the Bloodstones is vital to keeping Forsaken secrets from human hands.
For orcs, Lordamere recalls the years after the Second War, when thousands of their kin withered in captivity before Thrall rallied their people.
